video_title: AI Bubble Burst? Bitcoin to Zero? Hedge Funds Wrecked? Sounds Like a Bottom is Near
gist: Visser argues the late-October AI sell-off is a hedge fund deleveraging, compared with the 2007 quant quake, rather than a bubble burst, citing intact profits and claims and strong AI demand. He sees the unwind as nearly finished and pivots to healthcare, tokenization and Bitcoin, dismissing Chamath's quantum thesis.

themes.theme: Hedge fund deleveraging, not an AI bubble burst

insights.claim: Visser sees the current sell-off as one of the largest deleveraging events of his career, with the Goldman VIP crowded-long basket relative to the S&P giving back about half of its move since ChatGPT over 75 days.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Crowded-long unwind, not fundamental AI demand, is the driver of the drop.
insights.quote: the AI bubble didn't pop, hedge fund leverage did

insights.claim: Hedge funds entered the sell-off with a huge year-to-date head start, which changes behavior: they are protecting house money rather than trying to claw back losses, making de-risking more aggressive but also more finite.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Winners deleverage defensively; losers capitulate differently.

insights.claim: Visser judges the deleveraging to be either done or in the seventh or eighth inning, even though the market closed on the lows of the week, and expects a complete positioning reset heading into a new monthly performance clock in November and December.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Forced selling is largely exhausted, favoring a more neutral risk stance and a poor entry point for bears over the next 3 months.
insights.quote: the deleveraging is either done or in the seventh or eighth inning

insights.claim: Goldman data show stock pickers, quants and giant multi-strat firms losing more than 80 bps in a single day only three times since COVID, all in 2025-26 (Feb 4, July 28, Oct 15), with a bigger one occurring this week; global equity selling hit minus three sigmas on long liquidation.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Unwinds are recurring and accelerating in frequency, a sign of crowded books.

insights.claim: Thursday Oct 22 had the second-widest S&P 500 breadth-versus-price divergence since 1990 (324 stocks up while the index fell 1.36%), with only the DeepSeek day comparable; two-thirds of hedge funds finished down and Moderna and other big YTD winners were sold.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Selling was concentrated in crowded winners while the broad market held, which is a positioning signature, not a macro one.

insights.claim: Hedge funds were up 19% (systematic) and 8.8% (fundamental) year-to-date even after the worst days, so they are defending the month while still holding a chip stack, unlike 2022 deleveraging.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Less capitulation fuel than in years where funds were already losing.

insights.claim: Because index hedges (Nasdaq, S&P) no longer hedge AI exposure, funds short single stocks and baskets instead, pushing short positioning near a 5-year high and raising gross exposure rather than cutting longs.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: High shorts create squeeze risk once the unwind ends.

insights.claim: Visser compares the setup to the August 2007 quant quake: crowded exposure built over 18 months was unwound in about 75 days with no matching liquidity, and the quant quake saw near-full recovery after the factor unwind finished, unlike the July situational-awareness unwind which had no big bounce.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: If the analogy holds, a sharp rebound follows once forced selling ends.

insights.claim: The liquidity problem is in the long-short book, not AI names: AI stocks trade fine, but funds must buy back home builders and consumer staples shorts, producing the green screens on down days; $187B traded on Oct 22 in the top 50 versus far less in the bottom 50.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Short covering in unrelated sectors is a tell of long-short unwinds.

insights.claim: Visser argues AI destroys leverage through time: with agents and constant news, funds can no longer arbitrage time, so a stock can fall even if earnings beat for eight straight quarters, and multiples expand and compress much faster.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Strategies requiring months or quarters of drawdown tolerance are structurally impaired.
insights.quote: If your earnings beat estimates every single quarter for the next eight quarters, your stock can still go down.

insights.claim: Hedge funds, which historically lived on data and speed advantages as trend leeches, now compete with AI agents; only the largest retain a risk-management edge, which explains fund consolidation.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Expect further consolidation and tokenization to disrupt the hedge fund model.

insights.claim: Visser says markets will never again go six months without worrying, since hacks, geopolitical shocks and bad news will pop up constantly in the AI era.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Volatility regime stays elevated, favoring unlevered or long-horizon holders.

themes.theme: Contagion watch: France, Europe banks, credit

insights.claim: Leveraged fixed-income relative-value and carry trades in French bonds suffered big losses as the French-German 10-year spread hit 173 bps, near the top of its range outside the euro crisis, the worst week in 16 years of data.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Unwinds are spreading from equity into rates relative value.

insights.claim: European banks broke below their 200-day moving average and had their worst week relative to euro stocks since SVB; if this spreads into banks, more unwind waves could come from new places.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Watch European banks as the next contagion node.

insights.claim: Credit stress appeared in converts and CoreWeave, a neo-cloud IPO (Firmus) collapsed in Australia, and Microsoft pulled out of a data center; Visser reads these as capital-cost repricing rather than demand weakness.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Financing stress is the weak link, not end-demand.

insights.claim: Visser says the AI credit cycle has barely started: $10 trillion of capital is needed, free cash flow is negative because it was spent, and bringing massive financing to market quickly requires higher risk premiums.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Expect more debt and equity issuance and episodic credit scares.

themes.theme: Recession check: why this is not economic deleveraging

insights.claim: Visser distinguishes hedge fund deleveraging (earnings, margins and hiring still good, fast price decline) from economic deleveraging (profits fall first, then hiring, then prices); for the AI trade only the economic kind matters.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Use profits and margins as the real sell signal.

insights.claim: His recession model signals nothing now: jobless claims are stable or better than a year ago, S&P year-over-year is strongly positive, and corporate profits are still rising, whereas in 2007 profits turned down before the recession; the one warning is junk spreads, which made tights and are starting to widen.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Monitor junk spreads and year-over-year corporate profits for a regime change.

insights.claim: Since ChatGPT and the profit-margin surge, the S&P closed above its 20-week moving average 85% of weeks versus about 72-73% over the full history.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Structural bull regime with sharp but shallow corrections.

insights.claim: SMH is down 22% from its peak, which Visser calls a normal correction that happens nearly every year and that the semis are still up 30%+ year-to-date, with 85% of his tracked names still having upward-sloping 200-day averages.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Treat the drawdown as a bull-market correction unless earnings miss.

themes.theme: AI demand evidence and the capex case

insights.claim: SpaceX's earnings call said compute demand exceeds supply and that it could rent out compute several times over; Elon Musk targets an incremental 10 GW in 2027, which at 20-50B per GW-year Visser maps to 100-200B+ revenue even with haircuts; JPMorgan doubled its price target from 240 to 500.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Demand data from a supplier contradicts the overcapacity narrative.
insights.quote: compute demand is substantially greater than supply

insights.claim: Visser says a bubble is building capacity and hoping demand comes, while with AI the problem is keeping up with demand, so he sees no company guiding demand down in the earnings season so far.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Earnings guidance is the thing to watch to invalidate the bull case.
insights.quote: We can't keep up with customer demand.

insights.claim: He says Micron could reach 1500 by end of February and that bears should be careful given how little actual deleveraging has hit fundamentals, citing GPU residual values staying high and Taiwan and Korea exports still rising.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: A sharp bullish call on memory with high volatility.
insights.quote: by the time we get to the end of February Micron could be at 1500

insights.claim: Hyperscalers will not cancel capex because, per Eric Schmidt, no one wants to be seen in history as not participating in the biggest revolution, so no one finishes second or third.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Capex cuts are unlikely; arms-race logic persists.

insights.claim: Anthropic plus OpenAI revenue is described as going from roughly 28-29 (billion) a year ago to about 175 now, and slower growth quarters do not mean the trend is stopping.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: The transcript's units are garbled; treat the magnitude loosely.

themes.theme: Healthcare and specialized AI as next leg

insights.claim: Eli Lilly made new all-time highs; Visser calls it the most important AI company, citing TuneLab, a model trained on data from 135 biotech companies, and argues pharma, biotech and life sciences are beginning a major bull market with healthcare re-rating toward growth.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Add healthcare as a barbell leg alongside compute.
insights.quote: What is happening in pharma, life sciences, and biotech is beginning a massive bull market.

insights.claim: Humanoid robots, drug discovery and healthcare are expected to be part of next year's bull market, which Visser expects to feature many corrections.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Themes to position for in 2027.

insights.claim: Visser rejects Chamath's claim that quantum will send Bitcoin to zero, citing Adam Back that the quantum threat is 20-40 years away, that current machines cannot break Bitcoin, and that Bitcoin can upgrade, though the upgrade process may be slow.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Quantum is a hardware problem on a long timeline; he admits he is talking his book.

insights.claim: The nearer threat is AI agent swarms hacking banks, websites (70% of PHP sites broken into) and companies, which he expects to become the most important market story over three years and push banks onto blockchain.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Cyber crises are a catalyst for tokenization and crypto adoption.
insights.quote: what people should be worried about is not quantum hacking Bitcoin, they should be worried about AI hacking capitalism

insights.claim: A tokenized index of 46 names including Bitcoin is up 35% year-to-date and ahead of AI trades, and over 360 tokenized equity products exist on chain, up 200% year-to-date; JPMorgan has three tokenized products live on Ethereum and predicts Bitcoin outperforms stocks, gold and real estate over 10 years.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Institutional tokenization is accelerating; weekend tokenized-stock trading is already leading indicators of Monday opens.

insights.claim: Visser calls Bitcoin the purest AI trade, sees a multi-year bull market in tokenization, agentic commerce and stablecoins, and thinks Bitcoin breaking back above roughly 100,000 would unleash a significant move after two years of consolidation.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Crypto is becoming infrastructure for agents.

insights.claim: Tokenized AI stocks trading over the weekend front-run Monday and mean markets never sleep, so leveraged funds cannot rely on weekend gaps for adjustment.
insights.speaker: Jordi Visser
insights.so_what: Weekend tokenized trading adds a new stress transmission channel.
